sources.title: Discrete Lattice Material Vacuum Airship
sources.venue: AIAA SciTech 2019 Forum, AIAA 2019-0815; NASA NTRS 20190001133 (ARC-E-DAA-TN64902)
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted. Not the AIAA-typeset version.
sources.licenceReason: The NTRS record 20190001133 records distribution PUBLIC and copyright determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED, with belongsToPublisher false and containsThirdPartyMaterial false; the file stored here is byte-identical (MD5 5cada69db5e2f6ab7b2f361582d4e8c6) to the PDF NTRS serves, carries no AIAA copyright line and no arc.aiaa.org download stamp, and was produced by pdfTeX rather than AIAA's typesetting.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Redoing the classical vacuum-balloon analysis with an architected lattice whose modulus and strength scale linearly with relative density moves the binding constraint from stability to strength: solid, thick-shell and thin-shell designs all require a lattice constituent specific strength above 1,220-1,236 kN.m/kg, which current carbon composites (Toray M60JB, 1,979 kN.m/kg) clear by a factor of 1.6.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The only published lift figures for a lattice vacuum sphere. Table 2 gives 3,005,114 kg net lift at R = 100 m, which on a 1.225 kg/m3 basis means a shell of 0.508 kg per m3 of enclosed volume at every radius in the table. That is the number our ledger's dryT = payloadT bet (0.455 kg/m3) has to beat, and does not.

sources.title: Vacuum Balloon - A 350-Year-Old Dream
sources.licenceReason: The PDF's own first-page copyright block states 'This article is an open access article distributed under the terms and conditions of the Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license', with the licence URL, and MDPI Eng is a fully open-access journal.
sources.whatItEstablishes: A homogeneous single-layer evacuated sphere is impossible for any solid: floating and surviving together demand E/rho_s^2 above about 4.5e5, and diamond reaches only 1e5, so a perfect diamond shell buckles at roughly 0.2 atmospheres. A three-layer sandwich of boron carbide face skins on aluminium honeycomb does work, at a payload fraction of 0.1, with an ANSYS eigenvalue buckling safety factor of 2.65 and a minimum radius of 2.11 m set by intracell dimpling.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The payload fraction q = 0.1. It is the most rigorously checked published figure for what a vacuum hull costs, and it is 2.6 times heavier per cubic metre than our entire dry-mass allowance.

sources.title: Design of a Lighter than Air Vehicle that Achieves Positive Buoyancy in Air Using a Vacuum
sources.venue: MSc thesis, Air Force Institute of Technology, AFIT-ENY-13-J-02 (DTIC ADA587008)
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain. Distribution Statement A.
sources.licenceReason: The thesis title page carries 'APPROVED FOR PUBLIC RELEASE; DISTRIBUTION UNLIMITED' and was written by a serving officer (Capt. T. T. Metlen, USMC) at a US Department of the Air Force institution as part of official duties, so it is a work of the United States Government under 17 USC 105; AFIT Scholar hosts it as free and open access.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Defines W/B, the ratio of structure weight to displaced-air weight, and optimises three vacuum designs against it: a blade-stiffened isogrid sphere at W/B = 0.81 (0.79 with a beryllium skin), and a geodesic pultruded-rod frame at W/B = 0.57 which rises to 0.94 once a Zylon-reinforced Mylar membrane is added. A counter-rotating-cylinder concept was found infeasible.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The membrane penalty of 0.37, which is the term Jenett et al. and Akhmeteli & Gavrilin both leave uncosted, and the resulting W/B = 0.94 for the only design built from materials that exist.

sources.title: Design of a Structure that Achieves Positive Buoyancy in Air Using a Vacuum
sources.venue: 54th AIAA/ASME/ASCE/AHS/ASC Structures, Structural Dynamics and Materials Conference, AIAA 2013-1881
sources.licenceReason: Published in an AIAA conference proceedings behind arc.aiaa.org with no open-access statement on the item, and unlike the Jenett paper there is no NTRS or other government deposit of it.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The conference version of the Metlen thesis, and the paper Jenett et al. cite as reference [14] for the criterion that a homogeneous thin shell needs E/rho^2 above the order of 7.25e5 N.m/kg.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only - the thesis above carries the same results in more detail and can be hosted, so this entry exists to give the citation a reader will find in other papers' reference lists.

sources.title: The most severe imperfection governs the buckling strength of pressurized multi-defect hemispherical shells
sources.licence: arXiv default: arXiv.org perpetual, non-exclusive licence 1.0. Not redistributable by us.
sources.licenceReason: The abstract page's licence line resolves to arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/, which grants arXiv a licence to distribute and grants third parties nothing; research/README.md rule 3 says exactly this case is not redistributable.
sources.whatItEstablishes: In finite-element ensembles of pressurised hemispherical shells with lognormally distributed defects, the single most severe defect sets the buckling knockdown factor. Removing the least severe defects changes it by under 4%; a multi-defect shell has essentially the knockdown factor of a single-defect shell carrying only its worst flaw. Buckling is a weakest-link, extreme-value problem.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The reason the scale invariance our two structural sources assume cannot hold. Both hold shell mass fraction constant with radius; defect counts are not constant with radius, and the expected worst defect grows with the number of manufactured features.

sources.title: Buckling of Thin-Walled Circular Cylinders
sources.venue: NASA/SP-8007-2020/REV 2 (second revision of the 1965 NASA Space Vehicle Design Criteria monograph)
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted.
sources.licenceReason: NTRS record 20205011530 records distribution PUBLIC and determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED; it is a NASA Special Publication authored at Langley.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The current NASA design recommendations for buckling of isotropic and sandwich cylindrical shells under axial compression, bending, external pressure and combined loads, including the empirical knockdown factors derived as lower bounds to test data and the analysis-based alternatives developed by the NESC Shell Buckling Knockdown Factor assessment.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only, and that is the point: our hulls are thin-walled cylinders with caps under external pressure, this is the document that says how their buckling load must be established, and sim/ computes no buckling load at all.

sources.title: The kenemostat: Structural feasibility of a vacuum-buoyant geodesic vehicle including global buckling
sources.licenceReason: Crossref returns only Elsevier TDM and STM-ASF licences for this DOI and OpenAlex reports oa_status closed with no repository copy; ScienceDirect returns 403 to an unauthenticated fetch.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Not established here. The title and the fact that it treats global buckling for a vacuum-buoyant geodesic vehicle are all that could be confirmed from Crossref, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar; no abstract is indexed and the full text is paywalled.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Nothing, and it is catalogued to say so plainly. Our own prior concept paper cites it as reference [2] in support of the structural argument; nobody on this project has read it. It is the most recent peer-reviewed treatment of the one question that decides whether the vehicle exists, and it is the largest single gap in this collection.

sources.title: Analysis of a celestial icosahedron shaped vacuum lighter than air vehicle
sources.licence: © Elsevier. Not redistributable. An author preprint on AFIT Scholar is offered 'under the Elsevier user license', which does not permit third-party redistribution.
sources.licenceReason: Checked the AFIT Scholar record (scholar.afit.edu/facpub/848), which hosts the submitted preprint and states it is made available under the Elsevier user licence; that licence permits reading and text mining, not republication by a third party.
sources.whatItEstablishes: A finite-element and fluid-structure study of a celestial-icosahedron frame as a vacuum lighter-than-air vehicle, continuing the AFIT line of work begun by Metlen.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only. Catalogued so a reader tracing the vacuum-LTA literature does not have to rediscover the AFIT sequence.

sources.title: Finite Element Design and Modal Analysis of a Hexakis Icosahedron Frame for Use in a Vacuum Lighter-Than-Air Vehicle
sources.licenceReason: ASCE journal content is subscription-access with no open-access statement on this item; no government or repository deposit was found.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Frame design and modal analysis for a hexakis icosahedron vacuum LTA vehicle; cited by Akhmeteli & Gavrilin as one of the works that took the buckling question seriously.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only.

sources.title: Reversibly Assembled Cellular Composite Materials
sources.licenceReason: Science is subscription-access and this 2013 research article carries no open-access licence.
sources.whatItEstablishes: That discrete, reversibly assembled lattice building blocks can be joined into stiff cellular composite structures whose modulus scales linearly with relative density, which is the manufacturing route the vacuum-airship lattice argument depends on.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting only: it is why 'assembled from parts' rather than 'moulded in one piece' is the credible construction story for a hull this size. No number in sim/ comes from it.

sources.title: Ultra-Light and Scalable Composite Lattice Materials
sources.licenceReason: Wiley subscription article; no open-access or CC statement on the item.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Discrete lattice materials built from unidirectional carbon fibre reaching very low densities while retaining near-linear property scaling, and the manufacturing route for producing them at part counts that matter.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting only. It is the evidence behind Jenett et al.'s A = B = 0.1 ideal-lattice assumption, which is the single assumption their feasibility result is most sensitive to.

sources.title: Ultralight, Ultrastiff Mechanical Metamaterials
sources.licenceReason: Science subscription article with no open licence on the item.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Stretch-dominated microlattices whose stiffness scales close to linearly with relative density over three orders of magnitude, against the quadratic or worse scaling of foams and bend-dominated architectures.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting: it is the measurement behind the linear-scaling exponents alpha = beta = 1 that make the lattice vacuum balloon arithmetic close. Jenett et al. also take from it the caveat that strength scaling reverts to quadratic below a relative density of about 0.001.

sources.title: Mechanical metamaterials at the theoretical limit of isotropic elastic stiffness
sources.licenceReason: Nature research article, subscription access, no CC licence on the item.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Lattice architectures reaching the Hashin-Shtrikman upper bound on isotropic elastic stiffness at a given density.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only. It defines the 'ideal isotropic lattice' Jenett et al. assume exists when they evaluate feasibility, so it bounds how optimistic that assumption can be.

sources.title: M60J High-Modulus Carbon Fiber Data Sheet
sources.licenceReason: A manufacturer's marketing and technical datasheet carries no licence permitting third-party republication, and datasheets are revised without notice, so a stale hosted copy would be worse than a link.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The properties Jenett et al. and our own prior concept paper compute their margins from: tensile strength 3.82 GPa, tensile modulus 588 GPa, density 1.93 g/cm3 for M60JB.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting. The 1.6x margin on the lattice specific-strength requirement is this datasheet divided by that requirement. Our prior paper is right that datasheet fibre properties cannot be applied directly to a million-joint structure, and nothing in sim/ uses them.

sources.title: U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted.
sources.licenceReason: NTRS record 19770009539 records distribution PUBLIC and determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED; it is a joint NOAA/NASA/USAF publication and a work of the United States Government.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The idealised standard atmosphere: 101,325 Pa, 288.15 K and 1.225 kg/m3 at sea level, a 6.5 K/km tropospheric lapse rate to 11 km, g0 = 9.80665 m/s2, and a fixed mean molecular weight below 86 km that licenses a single specific gas constant of 287.053 J/kg.K.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The whole of sim/atmosphere.js, and therefore every lift figure published since defect 1 was fixed: rho = 1.1116 at the 1,000 m plateau and 0.9569 at the 2,500 m working altitude, the 22.2% growth in hull displacement, and the 5.25% float-up margin.

sources.title: Optimum Expanded Fraction for an Industrial, Collins-Based Nitrogen Liquefaction Cycle
sources.licenceReason: MDPI Entropy is fully open access and the article's own front matter carries the CC BY 4.0 statement; the PubMed Central deposit (PMC7597247) records the same licence.
sources.whatItEstablishes: For a realistic four-pressure-level Collins nitrogen liquefier, the optimum specific compression work is 430.7 kWh per tonne of liquid nitrogen at an 88% expanded flow fraction, against a reversible minimum of 173.4 kWh per tonne for the same change of state - a rational exergy efficiency of 40.3%, with about 40% of the destruction in the aftercoolers.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The evidence for CFG.eLN2 = 0.45 kWh/kg, which stands with a 4% margin on the conservative side, and the evidence against CFG.rtLN2 = 0.50, which does not: 0.50 x 450 kWh/t recovers 225 kWh/t from a liquid whose exergy is 173.4 kWh/t here and at most about 210 kWh/t anywhere in the literature.

sources.title: Photovoltaic Potential and Solar Resource Maps of Canada
authors: Natural Resources Canada, Canadian Forest Service
sources.venue: Natural Resources Canada / Federal Geospatial Platform, open.canada.ca dataset 8b434ac7-aedb-4698-90df-ba77424a551f
sources.licenceReason: The open.canada.ca package record for this dataset gives license_title 'Open Government Licence - Canada'; nothing is stored in papers/ because the item is a CSV data product on an FTP mirror rather than a document.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Mean daily global insolation by month and array orientation for over 3,500 Canadian municipalities. For July across eight British Columbia interior fire-belt municipalities the mean on a horizontal surface is 6.34 kWh/m2/day (5.87 at Prince George to 6.58 at Cranbrook), and 9.4 kWh/m2/day on a two-axis tracker.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The test of the solar term. sim/state.js applies 200 W/m2 of electrical output continuously; 6.34 kWh/m2/day is 264 W/m2 of incident energy averaged over 24 hours, so 200 W/m2 electrical implies 76% conversion efficiency. At 20% modules the same insolation gives about 53 W/m2.

sources.title: Missions and Vehicle Concepts for Modern, Propelled, Lighter-Than-Air Vehicles
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted.
sources.licenceReason: NTRS record 19850008448 records distribution PUBLIC and determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED.
sources.whatItEstablishes: A NASA survey of propelled lighter-than-air vehicle concepts and the missions proposed for them, with the sizing relationships, drag treatment and mass fractions conventional airship design uses.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting: the drag model in sim/physics.js treats the hull as a streamlined body of revolution with Cd = 0.05, and this is the tradition that number comes from. No figure in sim/config.js is traced to a specific page here, which is itself worth recording.

sources.title: Initial Feasibility Assessment of a High Altitude Long Endurance Airship
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted.
sources.licenceReason: NTRS record 20040021326 records distribution PUBLIC and determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED.
sources.whatItEstablishes: A sizing study for a solar-powered stratospheric airship, working through the coupling between hull volume, station-keeping drag power, solar array area and energy storage mass that decides whether such a vehicle closes.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting: the shape of our own sustainment problem. It is the closest published analysis of an airship that must generate its own power against drag, and it is the standard against which our 200 W/m2 solar assumption and per-cycle deficit should eventually be checked.

sources.title: Modeling and Simulation Tools for Heavy Lift Airships
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted.
sources.licenceReason: NTRS record 20160007347 records distribution PUBLIC and determinationType PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED.
sources.whatItEstablishes: What a heavy-lift airship simulation has to model to be credible, including the buoyancy management and ballast exchange problems that arise the moment a lighter-than-air vehicle picks up or sets down a large payload.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting, and a warning. It is the published statement of the ballast problem our descent anchor is an answer to, and it treats mass exchange as a first-order design driver rather than a detail.

sources.title: Aerial Firefighting Use and Effectiveness (AFUE) Report
authors: USDA Forest Service, Fire and Aviation Management
sources.venue: USDA Forest Service, 46 pp. (March 2020, posted August 2020)
sources.licenceReason: Authored by the USDA Forest Service and published on fs.usda.gov; a work of the United States Government under 17 USC 105.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Field observation of 27,611 drops at 272 incidents in 18 states, 2015-2018. Overall interaction percentage 89% and probability of success 0.82; but for airtankers used to halt fire spread, POS falls to 0.55-0.67, and for airtanker drops with no ground engagement POS is 0.56 against 0.72 with it, the most common single outcome without ground crews being 'not effective' at 26%.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The evidence that the metric this project publishes is the wrong one. AFUE measures whether a drop achieved its own tactical objective, never tonnes and never fire extinguished, and its ground-engagement split says an uncrewed fleet is operating in the least effective observed condition.

sources.title: Nationwide Aerial Application of Fire Retardant on National Forest System Land Biological Assessment for Fish and Wildlife Service Species - Addendum for Assessment of Effects Associated with Aerial Retardant Operations at Airtanker Bases
authors: USDA Forest Service National Technology and Development Program
sources.licenceReason: Prepared by the USDA Forest Service National Technology and Development Program and published on fs.usda.gov; a work of the United States Government under 17 USC 105.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Operational drop heights - 60 ft or more for single-engine airtankers, 150-200 ft for large airtankers, 300-500 ft for very large airtankers - and the Forest Service's own statement that 'a drop 1,000 feet above ground/vegetation level would completely dissipate' and that above 500 ft the majority of a jettisoned load dissipates before reaching the ground.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The direct contradiction of ALT.drop. Our ships release at 450 m above ground, or 1,476 ft, which is half again above the height at which the Forest Service says the load does not arrive, and three to five times the height a very large airtanker drops from.

sources.title: Rotor Wash
sources.venue: USDA Forest Service, Missoula Technology and Development Center, Wildland Fire Chemical Systems user guide sheet UG-15
sources.licenceReason: A USDA Forest Service MTDC publication hosted on fs.usda.gov; a work of the United States Government under 17 USC 105.
sources.whatItEstablishes: That helicopter downwash becomes a surface wind that can spread fire along the ground, and that a hovering UH-60 Black Hawk has to be well over 160 feet up before its rotor wash falls below 30 mph at the surface.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The first quantitative handle on the README's downwash question. Our P-10000 gives itself 79 kg/m2 of disc loading against the Black Hawk's roughly 47, on a disc some 450 m across, and sim/ models none of its effect on the fire.

sources.title: Airtankers
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain. No PDF exists.
sources.licenceReason: A US interagency federal web page; the text is a work of the United States Government. There is nothing to store because the item is HTML with no PDF edition.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The current US airtanker fleet by type and capacity - the operational baseline any claim about a new aerial suppression platform has to be compared against.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only, and it is a living page whose numbers change between fire seasons; anything taken from it must be dated.

sources.title: Interagency Wildland Fire Chemicals Policy and Guidance
sources.venue: USDA Forest Service fire programme pages
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain. Hub page, no single PDF.
sources.licenceReason: USDA Forest Service web page; a work of the United States Government. It links many separate PDFs rather than being one, so there is no single file to store.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The approval, qualification and use policy for retardants, foams and gels in US wildland firefighting, including the environmental constraints on where they may be applied.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only. This project drops plain lake water and adds nothing to it, which avoids this entire regime and should be stated as a deliberate choice rather than an omission.

sources.title: Bambi Bucket (collapsible helicopter firefighting bucket)
sources.venue: Product line, in service since 1983; now DART Aerospace. Inventor inducted into the US National Inventors Hall of Fame.
sources.licence: Manufacturer and foundation web pages, all rights reserved.
sources.licenceReason: Commercial product pages and a hall-of-fame biography; neither carries any licence permitting republication.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The collapsible suspended-bucket precedent our descent anchor claims: invented by Don Arney in 1978, first delivered 1982, in production from 1983, in capacities from 270 litres to 9,800 litres for heavy-lift helicopters such as the CH-47.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The 9,800 litre top-of-range figure behind the README's statement that commercial buckets top out near 10 tonnes. Our P-10000 anchor bag is 12,400 tonnes, which is 1,265 times the largest one ever built, and the precedent should be read as establishing the mechanism, not the scale.

sources.title: Quantifying snowfall from orographic cloud seeding
sources.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 117(10), 5190-5195
sources.licence: Published under the PNAS license. Free to read after six months; not an open licence.
sources.licenceReason: The article states it is published under the PNAS license rather than a Creative Commons licence, and the PubMed Central deposit is not flagged open access.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The first quantification of snowfall attributable to glaciogenic cloud seeding, from three isolated events in the Payette Basin, Idaho, in January 2017: total water generated of 1.2e5, 2.4e5 and 3.4e5 cubic metres, with ground gauges recording increases of only 0.05-0.3 mm of snow water equivalent.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context, and a scale check that cuts both ways. The largest seeded event produced 340,000 cubic metres of water; one P-10000 delivers 13,183 tonnes an hour, so it would take about 26 aircraft-hours to move the same water - which makes mechanical delivery look tractable and cloud seeding look small, and equally shows how little 340,000 cubic metres does to a landscape.

sources.title: WMO Statement on Weather Modification
sources.venue: WMO, approved by the Executive Council, 14 June 2025
sources.licence: © WMO. Personal non-commercial use only, no right to resell or redistribute.

sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only. This project moves water mechanically and makes no claim to modify weather; the statement is catalogued because our own prior concept paper reaches into that territory and this is the constraint on it.

authors: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
sources.venue: The National Academies Press, Washington DC
sources.licence: © National Academy of Sciences. All rights reserved. Free to download, redistribution prohibited.

sources.title: The Great Plains Irrigation Experiment (GRAINEX)
sources.venue: Bulletin of the American Meteorological Society 102(9), E1756-E1785
sources.licence: © American Meteorological Society. Free to read is not an open licence.
sources.licenceReason: AMS journals apply their own reuse licence rather than a Creative Commons licence, and no CC statement appears on this item.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The design and observations of the field campaign that measured how irrigating a large land surface changes the boundary layer and mesoscale circulation over it.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only, and the campaign the next four entries all report from. It is the closest existing evidence for whether putting water on land at scale changes the air above it.

sources.title: Influence of Irrigation on Diurnal Mesoscale Circulations: Results From GRAINEX
sources.licenceReason: The version of record carries '© 2022. The Authors. This is an open access article under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License' on its first page; the copy stored here is that version of record, retrieved from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln institutional repository because Wiley refuses unauthenticated direct downloads.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The first extensive observational evidence that irrigation modifies terrain-driven slope-wind circulations: irrigation in upslope regions weakens terrain-induced baroclinicity, which weakens the afternoon slope-wind circulation.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context. Applied water changes local circulation measurably, which is relevant background to any claim that delivering water to a landscape only wets it.

sources.venue: Journal of Applied Meteorology and Climatology 63(2), 245-262
sources.licenceReason: AMS reuse licence with no Creative Commons statement on the item; Unpaywall reports it closed.

Recorded here mainly as a correction: our prior concept paper cites this work under a title that does not exist ('...Characteristics in the U.S. Southern Great Plains'), with the wrong first initial and the wrong region - GRAINEX sampled southeastern Nebraska, not the Southern Great Plains.

sources.title: The size-distribution of Earth's lakes
sources.licenceReason: Crossref returns creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 for this DOI and Scientific Reports is a fully open-access CC BY journal; a corrigendum (srep42155, 2017) revises some fitted parameters and should be read with it.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Lake surface areas at or above 0.46 square kilometres are power-law distributed with a tail exponent near 2.14 and a fractal dimension near 1.4, close to percolation-theory expectations; below that threshold they are not.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting. sim/water.js picks a source by mapped surface area, and this is the distribution that area is drawn from - it says most candidate bodies are small ones, and that the largest lakes are a heavy tail rather than the typical case.

sources.title: The volume and mean depth of Earth's lakes
sources.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Verbatim non-commercial redistribution is permitted; we decline it.
sources.licenceReason: Crossref and Unpaywall both report CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. research/README.md admits only CC BY and CC0 to papers/, and this repository is served from a commercial domain, so hosting it would rest on our own reading of 'non-commercial' rather than on the licence being clearly compatible.
sources.whatItEstablishes: A volume-area scaling for lakes derived from the Hurst coefficient of Earth's surface, applied to a global lake census: total lake volume 199,000 cubic kilometres and overall mean depth 41.8 m, significantly shallower than the 62-151 m of previous estimates.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The method that would replace our surface-area proxy. sim/water.js treats mapped area as a stand-in for a lake being drawable; this paper gives a defensible way to turn that area into a volume, which means the proxy is a choice we have not yet justified rather than the only option. Read from the abstract and the published scaling description only, not from the full derivation.

sources.title: Water Sustainability Act, SBC 2014 c. 15, and Water Sustainability Regulation, BC Reg 36/2016
sources.licence: © King's Printer, British Columbia. Reproduction is permitted under the King's Printer licence with conditions; HTML only in any case.
sources.licenceReason: BC legislation is Crown copyright with a King's Printer licence that permits reproduction subject to conditions including non-alteration and an accuracy disclaimer; rather than reproduce a statute under conditions we would have to restate, this entry links to the authoritative text.
sources.whatItEstablishes: That in British Columbia unrecorded water may be diverted and used without an authorisation for firefighting, and that a fire department may divert, use and store water without an authorisation for activities related to firefighting preparation.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The legal half of the README's water question, and only that half. Drawing 10,000 tonnes from a lake to fight a fire is, on the face of the Act, lawful without a licence. The Act says nothing about whether the lake can stand repeated full-payload draws, which is the part that would actually break the logistics chain.

sources.title: Environment Baseline, Volume 4: Energy-Water Nexus
authors: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Policy and Systems Analysis

sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context. Our prior paper cites this as 'The Water-Energy Nexus: Challenges and Opportunities' with a 2017 date, which conflates two documents: that title is a June 2014 DOE report, and this is the January 2017 baseline volume that adapts it. sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context, and a useful yardstick: it is the only source in this collection that puts a defensible energy-per-cubic-metre figure on producing fresh water by any means, which is the natural comparison for our kWh per delivered tonne.

sources.title: Battery Cell-to-Pack Scaling Trends for Electric Aircraft
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted.
sources.licenceReason: NTRS record 20210017488 records distribution PUBLIC, copyright determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED and containsThirdPartyMaterial false.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The X-57 flight battery turned 225 Wh/kg cells into a 149 Wh/kg pack, a cell-to-pack factor of 0.66, and that factor worsens as cells improve: a 200 Wh/kg cell carries a 16 kJ core heat load and a 400 Wh/kg cell 32 kJ, so thermal-runaway containment mass grows with the energy density it is protecting.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The test of the battery specification. Every class carries 0.2 MWh per tonne of dry mass, so the pack alone demands 200 Wh/kg with nothing left for anything else; at the 149 Wh/kg NASA flew, the P-10000's 2,000 MWh masses about 13,400 t against a 10,000 t dry allowance.

sources.title: Energy Storage for NASA Missions
sources.venue: NASA Glenn Research Center, invited presentation to the ARPA-E IONICS programme review; NTRS 20205009101
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted.
sources.licenceReason: NTRS record 20205009101 records distribution PUBLIC and determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED.
sources.whatItEstablishes: NASA's pack-level ladder: state of the art around 250 Wh/kg at cell level, 300 Wh/kg at pack level 'achievable within reasonable timeframe', 400 Wh/kg 'will probably require maturation of all solid state', and 'no clear path for achieving pack specific energy greater than 500 Wh/kg'.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The ceiling. Even at 500 Wh/kg, the point NASA says it cannot see past, our battery specification consumes 40% of the dry-mass allowance, which the hull already exceeds on its own.

sources.title: From Cell to Pack: Empirical Analysis of the Correlations Between Cell Properties and Battery Pack Characteristics of Electric Vehicles
sources.venue: World Electric Vehicle Journal 16(9), 484 (MDPI); also EVS38 proceedings
sources.licenceReason: Crossref returns a CC BY 4.0 licence for the DOI and World Electric Vehicle Journal is fully open access; the copy stored here is the EVS38 conference PDF of the same paper, taken because mdpi.com returns 403 to curl.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Pack-level gravimetric energy density measured across real production battery-electric vehicles: LFP 125-145 Wh/kg, NCA 150-174 Wh/kg, NMC 140-180 Wh/kg, with cell-level gains translating into proportionally smaller pack-level gains as the passive-component mass fraction grows.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Independent corroboration of the NASA cell-to-pack finding from a different industry. About 180 Wh/kg is the top of the empirically observed production range, against the 200 Wh/kg our specification needs before the aircraft is allowed any structure.

sources.title: FOTW #1354: Electric Vehicle Battery Pack Costs for a Light-Duty Vehicle in 2023 Are 90% Lower than in 2008
authors: U.S. Department of Energy, Vehicle Technologies Office
sources.venue: US DOE Fact of the Week #1354, 5 August 2024
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain. HTML only.
sources.licenceReason: A DOE Vehicle Technologies Office article on energy.gov; a work of the United States Government. There is no PDF edition to store.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Estimated light-duty EV battery pack cost of $139/kWh in 2023 against $1,415/kWh in 2008, on a usable-energy basis in constant 2023 dollars at production scale of 100,000 units a year or more, from Argonne's BatPaC model.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context. This repository publishes no cost figure; the number belongs to our prior energy-as-cargo report and is recorded so that report can be checked.

sources.title: New Record Lows for Battery Prices (2025 Lithium-Ion Battery Price Survey)
sources.licence: © BloombergNEF. Proprietary commercial research, not redistributable.
sources.licenceReason: A subscription research product; the public page is a summary and carries no licence permitting republication.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Global volume-weighted average pack price of $108/kWh and cell price of $74/kWh for 2025, with stationary-storage packs at $70/kWh and the lowest observed pack at $50/kWh.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only, and it should be treated as a vendor-reported market survey rather than a measurement.

sources.title: Naxtra Battery Breakthrough and Dual-Power Architecture: CATL Pioneers the Multi-Power Era
sources.licenceReason: A corporate press release whose own page asserts all rights reserved.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Vendor claims for a sodium-ion cell: 175 Wh/kg, over 10,000 cycles, 90% usable power at -40 C, 5C peak charge.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context, and a caution. These are unverified manufacturer claims at cell level; 175 Wh/kg at cell level becomes roughly 115 Wh/kg at pack level on the X-57 factor, well below what our specification needs.

sources.title: QIJI Energy Heavy-duty Truck Battery Swapping Solution
sources.venue: CATL press release, 12 June 2023 (standardised 75# swap block announced 18 May 2025)
sources.licenceReason: Corporate press release asserting all rights reserved.
sources.whatItEstablishes: A deployed standardised battery-swap system for heavy trucks: 171 kWh blocks, one to three per truck, swap in a few minutes, stations holding 24 packs, more than 300 stations at the end of 2025.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context, and the only real-world precedent for the tender-ship exchange the README names as the intended answer to the energy deficit. It establishes that mechanical exchange at multi-hundred-kWh block sizes is in service; the fleet in this repository would need it at gigawatt-hour scale in the air.

sources.title: IEC 62840-1:2025 Electric vehicle battery swap system - Part 1: General and guidance; IEC 62840-2:2025 Part 2: Safety requirements
sources.licenceReason: IEC standards are sold through the IEC webstore and assert all rights reserved; neither part is available under any open licence.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The published international standard for electric-vehicle battery swap systems at up to 1,000 V AC and 1,500 V DC, covering interoperability interfaces, electric shock protection, EMC, communication security and marking.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context. It is the evidence that battery exchange has an agreed safety and interface standard at road-vehicle scale, which is the precedent our prior energy report leans on. Neither part has been read; both are paywalled.

sources.title: ANSI/CAN/UL 9540A, Standard for Test Method for Evaluating Thermal Runaway Fire Propagation in Battery Energy Storage Systems
sources.licenceReason: A proprietary UL standard sold through shopulstandards.com with all rights reserved.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The four-level cell, module, unit and installation test sequence used to characterise whether a battery technology undergoes thermal runaway and what fire and explosion hazard the resulting system presents.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context. It is the test regime a 2,000 MWh airborne pack would have to face, and the reason the containment mass in Chin et al. exists.

sources.title: Moving Beyond 4-Hour Li-Ion Batteries: Challenges and Opportunities for Long(er)-Duration Energy Storage
sources.licence: US Government-sponsored work, no copyright asserted.
sources.licenceReason: Produced by NREL under DOE contract DE-AC36-08GO28308; the report's notice page asserts no copyright and states it is available at no cost.
sources.whatItEstablishes: An analysis of when storage longer than four hours becomes economic, using a price-taker model with a round-trip efficiency of 85% over a year of hourly data.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting: the 85% figure is the standard modelling assumption for lithium-ion round-trip efficiency, which is the right comparison for our CFG.rtLN2 = 0.50 nitrogen store and shows how much worse a cryogenic store is than the battery it would displace.

sources.title: National Blueprint for Lithium Batteries 2021-2030
sources.licenceReason: Published by the Federal Consortium for Advanced Batteries on energy.gov; a work of the United States Government under 17 USC 105.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Five US national goals for 2021-2030 across raw material access, domestic materials processing, cell and pack manufacturing, recycling and reuse, and workforce.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context only. It is policy, not physics, and no number here touches sim/.

sources.title: NASA Electric Aircraft Testbed (NEAT) Summary of Capabilities, Version 3.0
sources.licence: US Government work, public use permitted.
sources.licenceReason: NTRS record 20250001338 records distribution PUBLIC and determinationType GOV_PUBLIC_USE_PERMITTED.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The capability of the largest facility built to test electric aircraft powertrains: 12 MVA available at 4,160 V, 3 MW of DC power installed, 2 MW of DC load banks, and an altitude chamber to 60,000 ft.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context, and a scale check worth stating. The largest electric-powertrain test facility in the world is rated at 12 MW; our P-10000 draws 150 MW of generation and 1,400 MW of battery discharge. Nothing exists that could test one system on this aircraft.

sources.title: Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure (Megawatt Charging System)
authors: U.S. Department of Energy, Alternative Fuels Data Center
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain. HTML only.
sources.licenceReason: An AFDC page maintained by NREL for DOE; a work of the United States Government. No PDF edition.
sources.whatItEstablishes: That the Megawatt Charging System is under development for DC charging up to 3.75 MW for short-dwell use, with lower-power charging below 500 kW for long dwells.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context, and a bound. 3.75 MW is the ceiling of the fastest conductive charging standard being developed; recharging a single P-10000's 2,000 MWh through one would take about 22 days, which is the arithmetic behind our prior report's conclusion that exchange must be mechanical rather than electrical.

sources.title: Hydrogen Storage
authors: U.S. Department of Energy, Hydrogen and Fuel Cell Technologies Office
sources.licence: US Government work, public domain. HTML only.
sources.licenceReason: A DOE EERE page; a work of the United States Government. The energy-density comparison is an embedded chart with no standalone PDF.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Hydrogen holds nearly three times the energy per kilogram of petrol (120 MJ/kg against 44) and roughly a quarter of the energy per litre as a liquid (8 MJ/L against 32).
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context. It is the reason our prior report rejected hydrogen as the energy carrier: an airship is volume-constrained before it is mass-constrained.

sources.title: Liquid Air Combined Cycle for Power and Storage, Final Report
sources.venue: Southwest Research Institute and Pintail Power for US DOE, award DE-FE0032002, report DOE-SwRI-0032002
sources.licenceReason: A final technical report delivered under a US DOE award and published without restriction on OSTI. One caveat recorded in its own caption: Figure 3 is marked as taken without permission from a third-party publication, so that single figure should not be reused.
sources.whatItEstablishes: That the widely quoted 439 kWh per tonne benchmark for air liquefaction is optimistic against engineering practice. A Wood Group EPC trade study for a 6,480 tonne-a-day train gives 685 kWh/t for a Claude cycle producing atmospheric-pressure liquid and 907 kWh/t for Linde-Hampson, which the report calls 'substantially worse than the initially assumed reference'. Adiabatic liquid-air storage with cold recycle reaches 297 kWh/t.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The boundary condition on CFG.eLN2 = 0.45 kWh/kg. Our figure matches the 439 kWh/t literature benchmark, but this report is the engineering study saying a real standalone plant making atmospheric-pressure liquid runs at 685 kWh/t. The lower numbers in the liquid-air literature all assume cold returning from a discharge cycle, which an aircraft making nitrogen from air does not have.

sources.title: Exergy-Based and Economic Evaluation of Liquefaction Processes for Cryogenics Energy Storage
sources.licenceReason: MDPI Energies is fully open access and the article carries the CC BY 4.0 statement in its own front matter.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Exergy and economic comparison of Claude, Heylandt and Kapitza liquefaction at about 2,946 tonnes a day: 263-264 kWh per tonne with cold storage against a literature range of 439 and 520-760 kWh per tonne without, and the finding that cold storage reduces specific power by 50-70%.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The size of the cold-recycle correction, which is what separates the optimistic and pessimistic ends of the liquefaction literature. Without a discharge cycle returning cold, the same processes sit at roughly 528-880 kWh per tonne - which is where an airborne nitrogen plant would sit, and is above our 450.

sources.title: Liquid air energy storage - Analysis and first results from a pilot scale demonstration plant
sources.licence: © Elsevier for the version of record; the repository accepted manuscript is CC BY-NC-ND, which the repository's rule does not admit.
sources.licenceReason: The publisher version is closed Elsevier, and the University of Brighton repository copy is an accepted manuscript under CC BY-NC-ND rather than CC BY or CC0.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Measured performance of the first pilot-scale liquid-air energy storage plant: cold recycle of 51% restricts round-trip efficiency to 36%, with a re-engineered build predicted to reach 49-60%. Low-grade heat was converted to power at 45% against 5-15% for an organic Rankine cycle.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context, and a caution about what the liquefaction literature can and cannot be cited for. The liquefier specific work is reported only as a graph, so this paper cannot be used for a kWh/kg figure despite being the obvious place to look.

sources.title: Transmission Service Rate Schedule 1830
sources.venue: BC Hydro rate schedule, effective 1 April 2026
sources.licenceReason: BC Hydro asserts copyright over its site content and publishes no licence permitting republication.

sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Supporting for our prior energy-as-cargo report, which prices charging a fleet against this schedule. Nothing in this repository publishes a cost.

sources.title: Powering B.C.'s Future: Market Signals Strong Interest in Providing New Capacity Resources
sources.licenceReason: A corporate news release; BC Hydro asserts copyright over its site content.
sources.whatItEstablishes: BC Hydro's current maximum generating capacity is 13.4 GW, with Site C now fully operational and adding about 8% to provincial supply; a call for expressions of interest drew 106 submissions totalling 19 GW.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The denominator for any fleet-scale energy claim in British Columbia. A single P-10000 at 1,400 MW of battery discharge is over 10% of the province's entire generating capacity, which is the number that should appear beside any statement about fleets of them.

sources.title: Transmission Connections for Large Loads
sources.licenceReason: BC Hydro site content, all rights reserved, and HTML in any case.
sources.whatItEstablishes: That a transmission connection 'can take years to plan, design and construct', with a system impact study alone taking about six to nine months and a facilities study a further six to nine.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context. The lead time on grid connection is the binding constraint on any base-station plan, and it is measured in years rather than in the months a fire season lasts.

sources.title: Our Clean System
sources.licenceReason: BC Hydro site content, all rights reserved.
sources.whatItEstablishes: BC Hydro's statement that over 98% of the power it generates comes from clean, renewable sources.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Context. It is the claim that makes a British Columbia base station attractive for an electric fleet, and it is a self-reported figure from the utility.

sources.title: Bambu PAHT-CF Technical Data Sheet
sources.licence: Manufacturer copyright; no redistribution licence offered.
sources.licenceReason: A vendor datasheet carries no licence permitting republication, so it is catalogued and linked rather than stored under research/papers/. The figures quoted from it are facts, not the document.
sources.whatWeTake: The only vendor-verified material properties in research/analysis/vacuum-cell.py. ISO 527 / GB-T 1040: density 1.06 g/cm3; Young's modulus 3860 +/- 230 MPa (X-Y) and 2180 +/- 130 MPa (Z); tensile strength 92 +/- 7 MPa (X-Y) and 47 +/- 5 MPa (Z). THE Z NUMBERS ARE THE ONES THAT MATTER: a pressure vessel is loaded in every direction and a filament-printed part is weakest across its layers, so the interlayer figure is what governs, not the in-plane figure a datasheet leads with.
sources.whereItCutsAgainstUs: It is the measurement that says no consumer printer reaches the material the concept needs. At 47 MPa and 1,060 kg/m3 the specific strength is 0.044 MN.m/kg against roughly 1.06 needed to float — a factor of 24 on the material, which becomes 9.8x on the shell once the tubular-strut architecture has done what it can.

sources.title: Mineral Commodity Summaries 2022 - Helium
sources.venue: U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2022, helium chapter (January 2022), prepared by Joseph B. Peterson (BLM)
sources.licenceReason: A USGS publication; works of the United States Government are not subject to copyright under 17 USC 105. The DOI identifies the whole Mineral Commodity Summaries 2022; pubs.usgs.gov serves the helium chapter as this standalone PDF, and the stored copy is byte-identical to it (sha256 in the prov file).
sources.whatItEstablishes: The 2021 US helium market: estimated Grade-A private-industry base price $7.57 per cubic meter ($210/Mcf), 'with some producers posting surcharges'; import sources 2017-20 Qatar 65%, Algeria 12%, Canada 11%, Portugal 7%; the Federal Helium Program still operating under BLM with 85.7 Mm3 of conservation helium remaining; and USGS's statement that hydrogen can substitute for helium in lighter-than-air applications where its flammability is not objectionable.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The baseline of the price series: $7.57/m3 is HE_PRICE_2021_USD_M3 in research/analysis/helium.py and the denominator of the +85%-in-two-years repricing the helium analysis leads with.

sources.title: Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024 - Helium
sources.venue: U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024, helium chapter (January 2024), prepared by Robert C. Goodin (USGS)
sources.licenceReason: A USGS publication; works of the United States Government are not subject to copyright under 17 USC 105. The DOI identifies the whole Mineral Commodity Summaries 2024; the stored copy is byte-identical to the chapter PDF pubs.usgs.gov serves (sha256 in the prov file).
sources.whatItEstablishes: The year the price doubled: estimated Grade-A price about $14 per cubic meter ($390/Mcf) in 2023, 'with some producers posting surcharges'; management of the Federal Helium System transferred from BLM to GSA on 2022-12-03; the two-lot sale in progress with bids due 2024-01-23; the 2023-09-07 lawsuit against the sale rejected 2023-11-02; lifting gas 16% of 2023 US apparent consumption (59 Mm3).
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The 2023 point of the price series (HE_PRICE_2024_USD_M3 is corroborated by this chapter and MCS 2025) and the middle of the Federal Helium System sale timeline the note carries.

sources.title: Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025 - Helium
sources.venue: U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025, helium chapter (January 2025), prepared by Robert C. Goodin (USGS)
sources.licenceReason: A USGS publication; works of the United States Government are not subject to copyright under 17 USC 105. The DOI identifies the whole Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025; the stored copy is byte-identical to the chapter PDF pubs.usgs.gov serves (sha256 in the prov file).
sources.whatItEstablishes: The 2024 US helium market: Grade-A base price about $14/m3 with producers posting surcharges; the Federal Helium System sold in two lots on 2024-01-25 (about 50 Mm3 of crude helium) to a single company and transferred 2024-06-27; the CHEU purification unit's lease lapsed 2024-08-11 and was unresolved at year end; the EU import ban on Russian helium effective 2024-09-26; world production 180 Mm3; US apparent consumption 56 Mm3 with lifting gas at 18%; import sources 2020-23 Qatar 40%, Canada 36%, Algeria 10%, Russia 4%; and the substitution sentence: hydrogen 'can be substituted for helium in some lighter-than-air applications in which the flammable nature of hydrogen is not objectionable'.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Every 2024 market constant in research/analysis/helium.py - price, US consumption, world production, lifting-gas share - and the raw material of the fleet-scale argument: 100 P-100 fills are 31% of US apparent consumption and 10% of world production, which is our arithmetic [calc] on this chapter's numbers. Its own footnote concedes the consumption figure is a USGS estimate over suspect Census export data, and it gives no age for the Federal Helium System - the '90-year buffer' phrase in helium.md is not from here.

sources.title: Using the jet stream for sustainable airship and balloon transportation of cargo and hydrogen
sources.venue: Energy Conversion and Management: X 3, 100016 (Elsevier, gold open access)
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 on the version of record per Crossref; the only copy we could obtain carries no licence line, so we do not host it.
sources.licenceReason: Crossref records the VoR licence as creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 and the journal is gold OA, but ScienceDirect refuses unauthenticated PDF download, and the only obtainable file - the Manchester Metropolitan University repository deposit (labelled CC BY 4.0 by the repository) - is an author manuscript whose own pages carry no licence statement and whose author list (five named) differs from the VoR's seven. Rule 3 wants the item's own licence line; a file we cannot match to the DOI we cite fails it. Catalogue only until the VoR is in hand.
sources.whatItEstablishes: A peer-reviewed proposal for hydrogen-filled airships and balloons riding the jet stream at 10-20 km to transport cargo and hydrogen; states that around 90% of reported hydrogen-airship accidents involved fire, and argues the fatality risk reduces considerably if operations are autonomous, ports are isolated, and low overflight of cities is prohibited. Read this round as the author manuscript, not the version of record.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The evidence that an uncrewed hydrogen airship is a live proposal in the literature - the competitor helium.md names as the open flank. It is a cargo-transit study, not a firefighting one: its safety-by-isolation levers are exactly what a fire ship gives up, and it does not touch certification, so it opens the question without settling it.

sources.title: A review of airship structural research and development
sources.licenceReason: Elsevier subscription article with no open-access statement; nobody on this project has read it - it is catalogued to say so plainly.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Not established here: paywalled and unread. It is reported secondhand to carry the ~1 L/m2/day helium permeability design requirement for airship envelope laminates.

sources.title: Novel Non-Evaporable Getter Materials and Their Possible Use in Fusion Application for Tritium Recovery
sources.licenceReason: The article's permissions block states the CC BY licence and it is printed in the stored PDF, so we may host a copy with attribution.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Non-evaporable getter alloys sorb active gases only (H2, H2O, CO, CO2, N2, O2) by chemical reaction — rare gases are not sorbed at all — with ST707 (Zr-V-Fe) carrying a hydrogen embrittlement limit of 20 Torr·L/g, and activation being a vacuum heat treatment.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The two facts that mass-rule getters out as air pumps for sealed cells: argon (0.93% of air) is ungettered, so the barrier must close the budget unaided; and even at the hydrogen-limit capacity, eating a 4,458 mbar·L decade budget takes >=167 g against a cell with 42 g of gross lift. Getters survive only as 0.5-2 g outgassing janitors. The paper is written for fusion tritium recovery; the application to airship cells is entirely ours.

sources.title: Improvement of quality of 3D printed objects by elimination of microscopic structural defects in fused deposition modeling
sources.licenceReason: The article's own copyright statement is the Creative Commons Attribution License, permitting unrestricted redistribution with credit; the publisher's typeset PDF is stored with full attribution in its .prov.json.
sources.whatItEstablishes: As-printed FDM walls leak gas through inter-road microchannels concentrated at coinciding perimeter seams: at extrusion multiplier k = 0.85 walls passed 24 mL/s of air at ~0.5 bar overpressure, flow reached zero only at k = 0.98, perimeter-only walls (~0.5 mm) often failed at every k, and walls of 1.1 mm and up sealed because a homogeneous inner layer closes the seam channels. Measured on PLA through a 0.30 mm nozzle at bubble-test sensitivity - mL/s, which is 9-10 orders of magnitude coarser than a vacuum leak budget.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The mechanism behind our position that the printed strut is structure, not the vacuum barrier; the k-to-1 extrusion calibration and the wall-thick-enough-to-bond-an-inner-layer rule; and the physical justification for a part-mass QC gate, since porosity and mass both track k. Its 'completely blocked' must never be quoted as vacuum-tight.
sources.load: as-printed walls are not gas-tight; k=0.98 threshold; mass QC gate (single source for the gate)

sources.title: Vacuum compatibility of 3D-printed materials
sources.venue: Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology A 32, 033001; arXiv:1308.4962
sources.licence: Journal version paywalled (AVS/AIP); arXiv posting under arXiv's non-exclusive-distribution 1.0 licence, which grants arXiv the right to distribute, not us.

sources.whatItEstablishes: SLS-printed PA12 polyamide outgasses at 3e-8 to 4e-7 mbar.L/cm2.s even after cleaning and a 24 h bakeout, with atmospheric residual gases indicating trapped air in the material; bakeout was limited to 65 C because a 100 C bake degraded the vacuum to ~1e-6 mbar and left residue. sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: Scaled to the 44 L demonstrator's ~0.75 m2 of internal printed surface, the polymer's own outgassing is 4-50x over a months-long hold budget with zero leaks - so the barrier film must isolate the printed polymer from the evacuated volume, or the protocol must bake and expect outgassing-dominated pressure rise in month one. The 65 C bake ceiling against PAHT-CF's Tg of 70 C is a bake-window conflict the demonstrator must test.

sources.licenceReason: Elsevier subscription article; catalogued with DOI, never copied.
sources.whatItEstablishes: Filament-wound composite lattice (anisogrid) cylinders as flight-proven primary structure - Proton-M and Angara interstages and payload adapters in serial production - with ribs running continuous fibre through every crossing, so the tube wall has no joints at all at that level.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The existence proof behind manufacturing route A (a jointless wound lattice wall). CAVEAT, carried in the note: this paper was catalogued from verified Crossref metadata plus secondary confirmation in the read papers and was NOT read for this round; scaling its cm-scale ribs to 100-300 um is this project's own order-of-magnitude extrapolation.

sources.title: Photonic Crystal Fibers
sources.licenceReason: Science subscription article; catalogued with DOI, never copied.
sources.whatItEstablishes: The stack-and-draw process: hundreds of capillaries fused into a preform and drawn into kilometres of fibre with the micron-scale hole lattice preserved - the most industrially scaled structured-cross-section process that exists, and geometrically exactly a tube whose wall is a lattice.
sources.whatWeTakeFromIt: The existence proof behind manufacturing route B (drawn level-2 cross-sections at km/day), with two caveats in the note: the process is silica/thermoplastic only - no continuous carbon can be drawn - and this paper was catalogued from verified Crossref metadata plus secondary confirmation, NOT read for this round.
